description:
Overview

The Commonwealth Shared Scholarship Scheme is a joint initiative between the UK Department for International Development and UK universities. It is designed for students from developing Commonwealth countries who have the ability to succeed at a UK university but would not otherwise be able to afford the cost of studying here.

At the University of Birmingham, the 2027 award covers the full cost of a one-year taught master's programme. That means tuition, a maintenance stipend at the UKRI rate, return air fare to and from the UK, the Immigration Health Surcharge, thesis expenses, a study travel grant, and an optical and dental allowance. It is a genuinely all-inclusive package, and it is worth noting that the award is tied to a small list of eligible master's programmes.

Applications for 2027 entry opened on 10 November 2026 and close at 16:00 GMT on 8 December 2026. Courses begin in September 2027.

Eligibility

The scheme has a narrow eligibility rule, so it is worth checking the basics before you commit to an application.

  • You must be a national of a developing Commonwealth country, and you must not be living or studying in a developed country at the time of applying.
  • You should not have carried out one year or more of study in a developed country.
  • You need to demonstrate financial need — that neither you nor your family could meet the costs of study in the UK without this award.
  • You must already hold an offer for one of the eligible master's programmes at the University of Birmingham.
  • You must meet the university's English language conditions, normally as a condition of your offer.
  • The award carries a return condition: when it ends, you are expected to go back to your home country to work or study. An extension to stay in the UK is only considered under special circumstances, typically when moving from the master's into a PhD.

Eligible programmes at Birmingham for this round are MSc Environment, Development and Politics; MSc International Development; MSc Respiratory Medicine; MSc Conflict, Security and Development; and MSc Clinical Oncology.

The nationality list covers developing Commonwealth countries. Examples include Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda; the complete list is published on the official scholarship page.

How to Apply

  • Apply for admission to one of the eligible master's programmes at the University of Birmingham.
  • Once you hold an admission offer, submit the scholarship application through the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission portal before 8 December 2026 at 16:00 GMT.
  • Link the scholarship application to your Birmingham admission offer, as the two are assessed together.
  • Provide evidence that you meet the university's English language condition for your course.
  • Upload all required documents and check that both the admission application and the scholarship application are complete before the deadline.

Because the window is short, it is sensible to start the admission application early and keep your academic documents and English test results ready.

Official Link

Important Notes

  • This scholarship is only for nationals of developing Commonwealth countries; applicants from other countries are not eligible.
  • The award has a return-to-home-country condition. Staying on in the UK is only considered in special cases, usually to progress from the master's to a PhD.
  • You need an admission offer before the scholarship application can be linked, so run both applications in parallel.
  • Always confirm the eligible programme list, nationality list and deadline on the official page before applying.
